neko.title: Neko Engine
neko.subtitle: Custom game engine with SIMD-optimized quaternion operations
neko.intro_text: During my studies at SAE Institute of Geneva in the Games Programming section, I worked on a custom game engine as part of a two-person team. This article presents an optimization I implemented using Intel Intrinsics to significantly improve quaternion performance.
neko.quaternions_text: Quaternions are used to represent rotations in 3D space. Based on complex numbers, they aren't intuitive to understand, but they're essential in game development. One of the main reasons we use quaternions is to avoid gimbal lock - the loss of one degree of freedom in rotation.
neko.task_text: My task was to optimize quaternion operations as much as possible, so I decided to use Intel Intrinsics functions to achieve this.
neko.basic_text: The basic implementation of quaternions looks like this:
neko.basic_explain: The quaternion contains 4 floats representing each value, and the Dot function calculates the dot product by multiplying and summing corresponding components.
neko.four_quat_text: To optimize the code, I created a new struct called FourQuaternion. Instead of doing calculations 4 times with different quaternions, we do it once by aligning values. We use 4 floats because they total 16 bytes - exactly what an XMM register can hold.
neko.aosoa_text: I approached the problem by creating an AoSoA system. Structures of Arrays separate elements into one parallel array per field, making it easier to pack them into SIMD instructions.
neko.alignment_text: The reason SoA is better here is because values are aligned in memory, making it faster to load all values in one block instead of accessing each individually:
neko.intrinsics_text: Intel Intrinsics are C-style functions that provide access to Intel instructions without writing assembly code. Here's the optimized Dot function:
neko.ps_explain: Packed single-precision floating-points (4 × 32-bit floats as a 128-bit value)
neko.load_explain: Loads 16 bytes from memory (4 aligned floats)
neko.mul_explain: Multiplies 4 floats with 4 other floats simultaneously
neko.add_explain: Adds 4 floats with 4 other floats simultaneously
neko.store_explain: Stores the result back to memory
neko.results_text: I created a test that calculates the Dot product of n quaternions using the MSVC compiler with an Intel Core i7 CPU on Windows 10:
neko.speedup_text: The FourQuaternion Dot product is between 3 and 4 times faster than the standard Quaternion Dot product - a significant optimization for real-time applications.
neko.assembly_text: Analysis on Godbolt showed the key difference: the standard Quaternion Dot function used jumps and movss (32-bit), while the FourQuaternion version used movaps (128-bit) with no jumps - confirming proper Intel Intrinsics usage.
